newsitem.title: SPAIN: BBV Q1 profits rise nearly 25 percent.
newsitem.headline: BBV Q1 profits rise nearly 25 percent.

text.p: Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya said on Thursday its first-quarter earnings rose nearly 25 percent, bolstered by strong gains in its Latin American business and from strength in traditional banking.
BBV said its attributable profit rose 24.8 percent to 24.73 billion pesetas in the first quarter in line with analysts average forecasts for a gain of 24.2 percent.
"The results reflect the success of our 1,000 day plan to reinforce our domestic position, which has been very good, and to export our know-how to Latin America," a BBV source said.
A Latin American shopping spree in recent months has put a strong shine on earnings, as analysts had expected.
BBV has bought the branch networks of Banca Cremi and Banco de Oriente in Mexico, while taking Colombia's leading bank Banco Ganadero and purchasing Banco Frances del Rio de la Plata.
Pre-tax profits from BBV's Latin American groups were 10.45 billion pesetas, compared with total pre-tax profit of 57.77 billion pesetas, BBV said in a statement.
Excluding Latin American holdings, net interest income would have risen just three percent and not the 24 percent registered.
Ordinary margin, which reflects loan, commission and own-account trading, would have risen 11 percent without Latin America instead of the 33.8 percent jump it registered overall, the source said.

Therefore, with costs growing at a rate beneath that of the ordinary margin, operating profits jumped well above expectations. Operating profits rose 41.2 percent to 76.84 billion against expectations for a rise to 69.61 billion.
But basic domestic business also performed well.
"Our business, in terms of both volumes and margins has gone very well," the BBV source said. "Investment funds continue to evolve favourably and commissions were strong."
